# zspark

LLM decoding for DGX Spark: GLM-5.3-Flash and Qwen3.8 Flash Next on the GB10, in Zig and CUDA.

zspark derives from [TensorFold](https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold) (Apache-2.0). It keeps TensorFold's CUDA
kernels and replaces the Python, PyTorch and Triton layers with Zig and CUDA C++; `zspark serve` is TensorFold
1.0.2's HTTP host, a dependency of the build, over zspark's own engine. There is no Apple or MLX support.

## Build

Needs Zig 0.17 and the CUDA 13 toolkit (`nvcc`) on a DGX Spark. The first build fetches CUTLASS 4.8.0 and
TensorFold 1.0.2.

```bash
zig build
./zig-out/bin/zspark probe
```

With a checkpoint directory (`nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4`):

```bash
./zig-out/bin/zspark chat DIR --no-thinking "List the first five prime numbers, separated by commas."
```

The reply streams to stdout; the reasoning and the timings go to stderr. `zspark chat` alone lists the options
(system message, a messages or tools file, sampling, `--render` to see the prompt without loading the model).
`--schema FILE` holds the reply to a JSON Schema and `--json` to a JSON object: every token is chosen among
those the document may go on with, drafted or serial, after the reasoning when thinking is on. A schema with a
keyword that is not read (`pattern`, `allOf`, `minimum`, ...) is refused by that keyword's name before the model
loads; `src/text/json_schema.zig` says what is read.

DIR may also be an EXL3 pack (`turboderp/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-exl3`), for every command (`chat`, `serve`,
`generate`, `score`, `compare`, `trace`, `info`) and with every `--kv-dtype`. Measured on spark-a, 2026-10-07,
one `generate` load a checkpoint (`tools/reference/readme_table.sh`):

| | EXL3 pack | NVFP4 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Load (`generate`), the page cache warm or empty | 10.7 s | 16.0 s |
| Device memory after a reply (`nvidia-smi`) | 50.9 GiB | 80.7 GiB |
| Host memory at its peak | 3.10 GB | 8.15 GB |
| Decoding, serial | 34.1 to 34.2 tok/s | 19.3 tok/s |
| Decoding, drafted | 63.7 tok/s, 100.8 to 112.4 on code | 49.9 tok/s, 77.4 to 87.1 on code |
| A prompt of 4055 tokens met for the first time | 4.99 s (812 tok/s) | 2.71 s (1496 tok/s) |
| `zspark score`, 5336 tokens of text | 2.161 nats | 2.150 nats |

The pack's 30 GiB n-gram table stays on the disk behind its mapping.
The load is the weights and the first reply's graphs, printed where `chat` prints `loaded in`. The reads are
direct and the pages are dropped after, so one start stands for the page cache being warm or empty. Prompt
windows are the session's: 512 on the pack, 2048 on NVFP4. Serial is that load's plain loop, the head not asked.

# zspark

LLM decoding for the NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121, 128 GB unified memory) in Zig and CUDA. It derives from
TensorFold 0.6.5 (commit 609ca41, the references' and recordings'): it keeps its CUDA kernels and replaces
the Python, PyTorch and Triton layers. `serve` is TensorFold 1.0.2's host, a build dependency (spec 059).
No Apple or MLX support, no Python at runtime.

## Scope

- Models: Qwen3.8 Flash Next (family `qwen4_exp` in TensorFold), built; GLM-5.3-Flash (`glm5_next`), next.
- Checkpoints: NVFP4 (`nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` as published, and the hybrid layout whose BF16 side
  layers are rewritten as 128x128-block FP8) and EXL3. MLX 4-bit is out of scope.
- Served: text, OpenAI chat completions, Responses and Anthropic Messages, streaming, tool calls, a reply held
  to a JSON schema or a required call; several requests at once with `--parallel`. The KV cache is bf16, FP8, or
  FP8 keys with NVFP4 values (`--kv-dtype`). Vision is a draft (spec 019).
- Two ranks (GLM needs them) go through NCCL, installed on its own.
- Python is allowed only under `tools/reference/`, in fixtures that export references from TensorFold.
